entries.name: Abstraction Laddering
entries.mechanism: move up (why) and down (how) to the right altitude
entries.when_to_use: Use when a problem is stated as a bare solution with an unstated purpose, as a vague aspiration with no concrete handle, when people are arguing past each other at different levels, or before committing effort at an altitude nobody chose on purpose.

entries.name: Affinity Mapping
entries.mechanism: cluster many notes into emergent themes (bottom-up)
entries.when_to_use: Use when a scattered pile of dozens to hundreds of existing items needs to become a few emergent themes, such as synthesizing user-research notes, support tickets, survey free-text, or retro stickies, and the right structure should emerge from the data rather than be imposed.

entries.name: After Action Review
entries.mechanism: expected vs actual -> why -> sustain/change
entries.when_to_use: Use when a project, launch, sprint, or incident has finished and you want to turn the outcome into learning, not a status update.

entries.name: Argument Mapping
entries.mechanism: diagram claim, reasons, co-premises, objections
entries.when_to_use: Use when an argument or recommendation must be evaluated for soundness, or when a fluent case may be hiding a broken inference.

entries.name: Assumption Reversal
entries.mechanism: negate foundational premises to generate options
entries.when_to_use: Use when an option space feels stuck inside default constraints, or when you need to expose premises that are taken for granted.

entries.name: Authentic Dissent
entries.mechanism: engineer for genuine minority dissent (not role-played)
entries.when_to_use: Use when consensus feels too easy, or to set up genuine challenge before a high-stakes call.

entries.name: Backcasting
entries.mechanism: from a desired future, work back to the path
entries.when_to_use: Use when planning toward a transformative or long-horizon goal that forward planning anchors too low, when a chosen future needs a route mapped back to today, or when milestones and dependencies between now and the goal must be made explicit.

entries.name: Belief-update routine
entries.mechanism: periodically revisit and update key beliefs vs new evidence
entries.when_to_use: Use when you hold consequential open beliefs, forecasts, or standing assumptions that should track new evidence over time and you want a disciplined, recurring re-score - not a one-time decision record, a finished-event retro, or a single claim's conditions.

entries.name: Boundary Critique (Critical Systems Heuristics)
entries.mechanism: audit the boundary judgments that define a frame (who benefits / decides / has expertise / has standing), contrasting the 'is' boundary against the 'ought' boundary and naming the affected-but-excluded
entries.when_to_use: Use when a plan, metric, or proposal already encodes who matters and who does not and the risk is solving a tidy problem for the people inside the line while pushing harm onto people outside it, when an improvement claim rests on an unexamined judgment about whose improvement, or on contested, value-laden, multi-party situations.

entries.name: Brainwriting 6-3-5 / NGT
entries.mechanism: silent parallel written generation + build-on
entries.when_to_use: Use when you need breadth of options and want to avoid the anchoring and conformity that make ordinary brainstorming underperform.

entries.name: Causal Layered Analysis
entries.mechanism: read an issue at four depths (litany / system / worldview / myth-metaphor), then reconstruct each layer into alternative futures anchored by a rewritten guiding metaphor
entries.when_to_use: Use when an issue is stuck because the framing is stuck, the official account and the system explanation have been argued to exhaustion, and the real disagreement is about clashing worldviews and the unexamined story underneath. Not a single-cause diagnosis (that is think-iceberg-model) and not a forecast.

entries.name: Causal Loop Diagrams
entries.mechanism: diagram reinforcing/balancing feedback loops
entries.when_to_use: Use when a situation feeds back on itself - growth that funds more growth, a fix that recreates its own problem, capacity that relieves then re-attracts demand - and you need to see why it keeps accelerating, stalling, or overshooting. Not for a single accumulation, a one-directional consequence tree, or a genuinely linear chain.

entries.name: Concept Mapping
entries.mechanism: diagram concepts and labeled relationships
entries.when_to_use: Use when a domain has many interrelated concepts and the goal is to externalize and inspect how they relate, forcing every relationship to be named rather than left as a vague association.

entries.name: Consider the unknowns
entries.mechanism: before committing to a judgment, explicitly list the relevant variables you cannot observe and weigh the gap they leave
entries.when_to_use: Use when a consequential one-off judgment rests on thin or partial evidence, no usable base rate exists, and the confidence on the table may be inflated by what was never looked at. Not for cases with a real reference class, for widening a numeric interval, or for unknowns cheap enough to just go resolve.

entries.name: Contradiction Resolution (Ideal Final Result)
entries.mechanism: reframe a trade-off as a contradiction to dissolve (separation in time/space/scale/condition), anchored to an implementation-free Ideal Final Result
entries.when_to_use: Use when a decision has hardened into an either/or like speed versus quality, thorough versus fast, or generous versus profitable, when splitting the difference feels wrong and a win-win would be worth far more than the best compromise, or when a recurring design or product trade-off keeps forcing the same painful balance.

entries.name: Contradiction / Tension Mapping (Polarity Mapping)
entries.mechanism: map an unsolvable polarity as both/and rather than smoothing it - name the two interdependent poles, the upside and downside of each, the greater purpose that makes managing both worthwhile, plus early-warning signs and action steps for staying in the productive zone
entries.when_to_use: Use when an organization keeps oscillating destructively between two opposites that are both true and interdependent (centralize versus decentralize, stability versus change, candor versus diplomacy), and treating each swing as a problem to solve is the actual mistake. Not for a dissolvable trade-off and not for a real either/or choice.

entries.name: Decision Journal
entries.mechanism: record decision + expectation + confidence for calibration
entries.when_to_use: Use when committing to a consequential, uncertain decision (a launch, hire, investment, bet, or strategic choice) and you want to lock in the prediction now to defeat hindsight bias and build calibration, or when pairing a record-now step with a later review.

entries.name: Decision Option Review
entries.mechanism: compare options against weighted criteria
entries.when_to_use: Use when choosing among several real options, or when a decision needs its tradeoffs made explicit rather than left to intuition.

entries.name: Dialectical bootstrapping
entries.mechanism: estimate, assume the estimate is wrong and list why, estimate again from those changed assumptions, then average the two numbers
entries.when_to_use: Use when a hard, one-off, bounded-scale numeric estimate (a year, a percentage, a count, a forecast) is about to be committed and no second judge, no real reference class, and no better data are available. Not for easy questions, not for unbounded order-of-magnitude unknowns, and never a cherry-picked single number in place of the average.
aliases: wisdom of many in one mind

entries.name: Ethical Matrix
entries.mechanism: grid affected parties (rows, including voiceless ones) against prima facie principles (wellbeing, autonomy, fairness) and read the cell-level pattern of trade-offs
entries.when_to_use: Use when a concrete proposal affects multiple parties with a genuine moral trade-off among them, some affected parties have no voice, and an ethics debate keeps sliding between groups and principles. Not a decision calculator and not an option-versus-criteria scorer; the matrix maps the terrain and leaves the weighing to deliberation.

entries.name: Evidence vs Inference Sort
entries.mechanism: label claims evidence / inference / assumption
entries.when_to_use: Use when a recommendation must be trusted, or when you need to audit the reasoning behind a conclusion in a high-stakes context.

entries.name: Expected-value / decision-tree
entries.mechanism: price the uncertainty: a tree of choice and chance nodes, rolled back to an expected value per option, with a what-flips-it sensitivity note
entries.when_to_use: Use when a decision turns on uncertain outcomes you can put rough probabilities on, when the structure is sequential (a choice opens chance events that open later choices), and when the stakes justify making the probability assumptions explicit and inspectable instead of buried in a gut feel.

entries.name: Far-analogy ideation
entries.mechanism: transfer deep structure from distant domains
entries.when_to_use: Use when near, obvious solutions are exhausted and you need genuinely original approaches.

entries.name: Fermi estimation
entries.mechanism: structured order-of-magnitude estimate from decomposition
entries.when_to_use: Use when you need a number and no lookup-able data or genuine reference class exists, so the magnitude has to be built from factors (for example sizing a market, a load, a cost, or a conversion you cannot look up). Not for forecasting from real base rates (use reference-class-forecasting) or decomposing a question for coverage with no number (use issue-tree).

entries.name: Frame Creation
entries.mechanism: reframe the problem by distilling themes and the core paradox, then abduce a new standpoint (often an 'approach it as if it were Y' analogy) and reason forward to solutions
entries.when_to_use: Use when an open paradoxical problem keeps resisting solutions inside the frame it arrived in, when conventional problem solving has only produced more of the symptom, or when the way a problem is framed is itself the obstacle and a fresh standpoint would be worth more than another solution attempt.

entries.name: Futures Wheel
entries.mechanism: map first/second/third-order consequences outward
entries.when_to_use: Use when a decision has knock-on effects over time, or when first-order thinking is missing downstream risks and opportunities.

entries.name: Iceberg Model
entries.mechanism: events -> patterns -> structures -> mental models
entries.when_to_use: Use when a problem keeps recurring despite event-level fixes, when a symptom is being treated as a one-off, or when the question is why this keeps happening and where to actually intervene.

entries.name: Interest-based negotiation (BATNA / principled negotiation)
entries.mechanism: separate both sides' interests from their positions, decide against your BATNA inside the mapped ZOPA, and invent options for mutual gain across differently-valued issues before dividing value
entries.when_to_use: Use when agreement is required from a party not under your control and more than one issue is in play (salary, vendor, partnership, resource, or multi-party disputes), and a position fight has hardened before anyone checked whether the interests actually conflict. Preparation deskwork only, not live-table tactics, and not for a single-issue distributive haggle or a choice with no counterparty.

entries.name: Interval calibration check
entries.mechanism: test a stated confidence interval against an equivalent bet, widen until indifferent, then score stated confidence against the actual hit rate wherever outcomes resolve
entries.when_to_use: Use when a human-stated interval or confidence number drives a consequential plan, forecast, or commitment and has never been audited, and the worry is overprecision rather than a wrong central estimate. Calibrates human-stated uncertainty only, never the agent's own confidence, and resizes width without relocating the number. Not for lookupable facts and not a promise of full debiasing.

entries.name: Issue Trees
entries.mechanism: decompose a question into a MECE tree
entries.when_to_use: Use when a question is too broad or multi-cause to answer as posed (for example "why is churn rising?", "where is margin leaking?", "should we launch a free tier?"), when analysis work must be split into non-overlapping parts, or when coverage matters and missing a whole category would be costly. Not for evaluating a given argument's soundness (use argument-mapping) or clustering existing notes (use affinity-mapping).

entries.name: Ladder of Inference Check
entries.mechanism: reconstruct the climb from data to conclusion
entries.when_to_use: Use when a conclusion feels certain but rests on interpretation, or to audit a contested inference.

entries.name: Mechanical / linear-model aggregation
entries.mechanism: combine cues with a simple fixed formula instead of holistic judgment
entries.when_to_use: Use when the same kind of evaluative judgment recurs (screening candidates, scoring leads, triaging) and gut calls are inconsistent or overconfident.

entries.name: Minimax regret
entries.mechanism: minimize worst-case regret: build a regret (opportunity-loss) matrix over un-probabilized states and choose the option whose maximum regret is smallest
entries.when_to_use: Use when a few discrete options face a few discrete uncontrollable states and no defensible probabilities exist. Not an expected-value tree (which needs probabilities) and not an attribute scorecard.

entries.name: Morphological analysis
entries.mechanism: enumerate the solution space by parameter combination, then prune to the internally consistent configurations (cross-consistency assessment)
entries.when_to_use: Use when a solution is genuinely a configuration - a choice on each of several semi-independent dimensions (product architecture, service bundle, policy package) - and the risk is defaulting to one familiar combination and never seeing the rest of the space. Not a top-down MECE tree and not a provoked option list.

entries.name: Natural-frequency Bayesian framing
entries.mechanism: re-express conditional probabilities as frequencies
entries.when_to_use: Use when interpreting a test result, screening signal, or any "given a positive, what is the real probability" question.

entries.name: One-way vs Two-way Door
entries.mechanism: classify by reversibility, match deliberation
entries.when_to_use: Use when it is unclear how much process a decision deserves, when a team is about to rubber-stamp something irreversible or convene a committee over something trivially reversible, or when a chronically slow org needs a defensible reason to move fast or slow down.

entries.name: Pairwise comparison
entries.mechanism: rank when you cannot score: judge items two at a time, tally the binary wins into a comparison matrix, and derive an order without an absolute scale
entries.when_to_use: Use when items must be ranked but no defensible scale or articulable criteria exist. Not a criteria-weighted option matrix and not a base-rate forecast.

entries.name: Parallel Perspectives Review
entries.mechanism: examine a decision through separated lenses (facts/upside/risk/intuition/alternatives/process)
entries.when_to_use: Use when a choice needs a rounded look, or when risk-aversion or optimism is drowning out the other perspectives.

entries.name: Premortem
entries.mechanism: imagine the plan failed, work back to causes
entries.when_to_use: Use when about to commit to a launch, hire, investment, migration, or any risky, hard-to-reverse decision, or when you need risks surfaced before committing.

entries.name: Problem Restatement
entries.mechanism: rewrite the problem several ways, pick a better frame
entries.when_to_use: Use when a problem is vague, arrived as a symptom or a pre-baked solution, or before committing significant work to solving the wrong thing.

entries.name: Process tracing
entries.mechanism: test rival causal explanations of a single case by each piece of evidence's diagnosticity (hoop, smoking-gun, straw-in-the-wind, doubly-decisive tests)
entries.when_to_use: Use when one outcome has happened, several genuine rival explanations compete to explain it, and mechanism-level evidence (logs, timestamps, documents, who knew what when) is available to discriminate them - an incident postmortem, a churn spike, a lost deal, a metric anomaly. Not for cross-case generalization, not a consistency-matrix scoring tally, and not for cases with no rivals on the table.

entries.name: Pyramid Principle
entries.mechanism: answer-first governing thought + grouped support
entries.when_to_use: Use when a conclusion or recommendation already exists and must be communicated clearly to a busy or senior reader, when findings need to be ordered into a tight top-down case, or when a write-up buries its point under context.

entries.name: Question Burst
entries.mechanism: rapid questions-only burst, then rank + pick
entries.when_to_use: Use when you are stuck, too attached to one framing, or need a better question before answering.

entries.name: Red Team / Blue Team
entries.mechanism: construct the strongest adversarial case against a thesis
entries.when_to_use: Use when a plan has too-easy consensus and needs pressure-testing, or to steelman the opposition before committing.

entries.name: Reference Class Forecasting
entries.mechanism: anchor an estimate on the base rate of comparable cases
entries.when_to_use: Use when forecasting cost, time, or odds of success for a project prone to optimism or the planning fallacy.

entries.name: Role-storming
entries.mechanism: generate divergent ideas while inhabiting a chosen non-self persona, using the identity as an inhibition-lowering and distancing lens
entries.when_to_use: Use when idea flow is throttled by self-consciousness or a fixated frame rather than missing knowledge, and you want more and stranger candidates before converging. Not evaluation through fixed lenses (that is parallel-perspectives) and not genuine challenge (that is authentic-dissent).

entries.name: SCAMPER
entries.mechanism: seven transformation prompts on a seed idea
entries.when_to_use: Use when you have a seed idea and need to break past the obvious options; not for blank-page ideation.
aliases: Substitute Combine Adapt Modify Put-to-other-use Eliminate Reverse

entries.name: Scenario planning
entries.mechanism: construct a set of divergent, internally consistent external futures (2x2 critical-uncertainty axes), then robustness-test strategy across them
entries.when_to_use: Use when the planning horizon is long and the decisive forces are outside control and not reliably predictable, and a single implicit forecast is driving the strategy. Not forecasting and not a single preferred path.

entries.name: Speculative harms and anti-goals
entries.mechanism: assume the design succeeds at scale, narrate the dystopian near-future in which it harms third parties and is exploited in bad faith, then convert each harm into an explicit anti-goal constraining the design
entries.when_to_use: Use when a feature's success case could externalize harm onto people outside the customer relationship (location, ranking, inference, targeting, automation) and the team's risk review is entirely project-centric. Not a premortem (route plan-survival risk there), not for present documented harms (route to incident analysis), and not a security threat model.

entries.name: Stocks and Flows reasoning
entries.mechanism: reason about accumulations and rates
entries.when_to_use: Use when a problem involves an accumulation (cash, debt, backlog, headcount, customer base, technical debt, emissions) and intuition about whether it is rising or falling may be wrong.

entries.name: Theory of Constraints
entries.mechanism: find the single binding constraint capping throughput and attach its exploit / subordinate / elevate decisions (the five focusing steps)
entries.when_to_use: Use when a system has a clear flow (a pipeline, a funnel, a queue, an approval chain, a production line) whose output is capped by one step and improvement effort is being spread evenly across all steps instead of aimed at the bottleneck. Not for coverage questions (route to think-issue-tree), recurring deep-cause questions (route to think-iceberg-model), or accumulation-trajectory questions (route to think-stocks-and-flows-reasoning).

entries.name: Three Horizons
entries.mechanism: hold three overlapping change curves (declining present H1, contested transition H2, emerging desired future H3) on one time canvas, locate the actor, and read the transition dynamics
entries.when_to_use: Use when a group is stuck in a present-versus-future binary and needs to govern the managed decline of the old system and the cultivation of the new one at once. Not a single backward path from one fixed future, and not a set of ranked external futures.

entries.name: Veil-of-ignorance reasoning
entries.mechanism: decide a values trade-off as if you had an equal chance of being any affected party, then return to the actual decision and confront the gap
entries.when_to_use: Use when a decision distributes benefit and burden across parties, the decider is one of those parties, and the risk is a self-serving call dressed as fairness. Not a neutral verdict, not forecasting, and not for cases where desert, promises, or compensatory claims make identity morally load-bearing.

entries.name: Argumentation schemes with critical questions
entries.mechanism: identify which stereotyped argument pattern is in play, then test it with that scheme's standard critical questions
entries.when_to_use: Use when a single presumptive argument rests on an authority's say-so, a load-bearing analogy, a slippery-slope objection, or a consequence-based case, and the question is whether its presumption survives the standard defeaters for that pattern. Not for structurally complex multi-premise arguments (use argument-mapping) and not for deductive or statistical proof.

entries.name: What Would Have to Be True
entries.mechanism: turn a claim into testable conditions
entries.when_to_use: Use when evaluating a strategic bet, or when a disagreement has become a clash of opinions rather than evidence.

entries.name: WOOP / MCII
entries.mechanism: wish-outcome-obstacle-plan with an if-then
entries.when_to_use: Use when a goal is already chosen but follow-through keeps failing, or to close the gap between intention and action.

entries.name: Framework Advisor
entries.mechanism: Produces a prioritized, evidence-graded Thinking Plan that diagnoses which thinking frameworks a situation actually needs - the dominant cognitive job, a short sequence of the fewest fitting frameworks to apply (each with its evidence tier, expected artifact, and a ready-to-run prompt), and what not to use.
entries.when_to_use: Produces a prioritized, evidence-graded Thinking Plan that diagnoses which thinking frameworks a situation actually needs - the dominant cognitive job, a short sequence of the fewest fitting frameworks to apply (each with its evidence tier, expected artifact, and a ready-to-run prompt), and what not to use. Recommends only frameworks this library ships. Use when unsure which thinking method or skill fits a decision, problem, or stuck point, when overwhelmed by where to start, or when you need a recommended plan of which frameworks to use and why rather than running one yourself.

entries.name: Random Frameworks
entries.mechanism: Generates three off-pattern framework analyses of a topic by drawing frameworks at random, applying each regardless of fit, and harvesting the non-obvious angles the unexpected lenses expose.
entries.when_to_use: Generates three off-pattern framework analyses of a topic by drawing frameworks at random, applying each regardless of fit, and harvesting the non-obvious angles the unexpected lenses expose. Use when a framing feels frozen or fixated and the goal is to break out of it with deliberately unranked methods rather than the obvious best-fit ones. Use when relevance-ranked selection would only reinforce the stuck view and a random draw is wanted to surface what a fitted analysis would miss.

entries.name: Research Framework
entries.mechanism: Researches a thinking framework end to end and produces a schema-valid proposed registry entry plus a learning dossier, grading the evidence on the seven-tier model and assessing overlap against the shipped catalog.
entries.when_to_use: Researches a thinking framework end to end and produces a schema-valid proposed registry entry plus a learning dossier, grading the evidence on the seven-tier model and assessing overlap against the shipped catalog. Use when you need an honest evidence grade and a build-or-fold verdict for a candidate method before turning it into a skill, when reproducing the evidence-and-overlap vetting on a method the catalog already judged, or when you need a ranked shortlist of new candidate methods in a family.

entries.name: Top3
entries.mechanism: Produces a worked three-framework analysis of a topic.
entries.when_to_use: Produces a worked three-framework analysis of a topic. Ranks the library's thinking frameworks for relevance, applies the top three so each emits its real artifact, and reconciles them into one cross-framework synthesis. Use when a decision, problem, or stuck point deserves more than one lens and the goal is worked output now rather than a plan of which methods to run later. Use when several frameworks plausibly fit and the most relevant few should be ranked, executed, and integrated into a single read.

entries.name: Audit Reasoning
entries.when_to_use: Check whether a conclusion is sound before trusting it, by sorting evidence from inference, reconstructing the inferential climb, and reviewing through separated lenses.

entries.name: Expand Options
entries.when_to_use: Break past the obvious option set by reframing the problem, transforming the seed with SCAMPER, and reversing its foundational assumptions, then shortlisting candidates.

entries.name: First Principles
entries.when_to_use: Reason from fundamentals by decomposing a problem to its irreducible level, then stripping the inherited assumptions, so you rebuild from what is actually necessary rather than from convention or analogy.

entries.name: Idea Quality Audit
entries.when_to_use: Decide which of a batch of candidate ideas are worth committing to, by scoring them on explicit quality dimensions and then adversarially stress-testing the strongest few.

entries.name: Issue Position Argument Mapping
entries.when_to_use: Turn a tangled multi-question deliberation or transcript into an inspectable typed map by chaining shipped moves, surfacing the open issues, attaching rival positions to each, and running a pro/con pass on each position, so a sprawling debate becomes a navigable structure.

entries.name: Kepner Tregoe
entries.when_to_use: Run the Kepner-Tregoe rational process as a chain of shipped moves, taking a bounded operational problem through cause-finding, then a weighted choice among options, then a forward risk pass, so a fix is de-risked end to end.

entries.name: Pdca A3
entries.when_to_use: Run the Plan-Do-Check-Act improvement loop as a chain of shipped moves, taking a performance gap through root-cause and countermeasure choice, then a structured review of actual versus expected, then a standardize-or-iterate decision.

entries.name: Reframe Problem
entries.when_to_use: Make sure you are solving the right problem before generating solutions, by restating it, sorting evidence from inference, and reviewing it through separated lenses.

entries.name: Stress Test Decision
entries.when_to_use: Pressure-test a consequential decision before committing, by comparing options, surfacing the conditions that must hold, imagining failure, and sanity-checking the estimate against base rates.
